A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLM-Transformer study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite relocation of supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLM and EIF simulations, comparative robustness experiments, ablations and analysis of Allen Institute neural recordings.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a four-population EIF simulation and supplementary six-area neural-activity outputs.

M1.justification: The Transformer VAE, spline decoder, low-rank coupling, post-spike filters, regularization and four-stage training remain unchanged. Expanded component explanations and suggested future variable-length decoders do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds an EIF scenario with chained and branching connections: 1→2→3 and 1→4. The original GLM simulations and Allen dataset remain. Figure S4 expands reporting for the six visual areas already studied in v1.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains RRR, mDLAG, single-neuron GLMs with and without trial-wise gain, and the GLM-Transformer variant without trial-varying dynamics. Table S1 retains the same encoder replacement and component-removal variants.

E3.justification: The added EIF experiment evaluates four groups of 50 neurons, with specified directed connections and estimates for every inter-group pair. Existing splits, preprocessing and tuned settings remain unchanged. Table S1's altered numerical scale is not explained as a protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a targeted scalability and connectivity-recovery check. Section 3 also newly reports stable performance for 10–20 ms encoder bins and slight degradation outside that range. Existing ablations, non-identifiability examples and shared-background robustness tests remain.

E5.justification: Table S1 removes the convention reporting small standard errors only as '<0.0001' and supplies explicit scientific-notation values. This improves reporting precision, without documenting additional runs, seeds, uncertainty estimators or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures S3–S4 add connectivity-recovery and six-area outputs. Table S1 replaces its numerical entries; for example, full-model GLM NLL changes from 0.2006 to 3.008×10^7. The unexplained scale change cannot establish a performance gain. The full model remains best in each ablation column.

T1.justification: The model equations, regularization formula and EIF dynamics are retained. The timescale-separation assumption receives additional motivation but is not mathematically revised. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the claims of interpretable directed coupling, robustness to background fluctuations, scalability and recovery of plausible visual pathways. Added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 newly states that convergence typically requires over a thousand trials, roughly an order of magnitude more than traditional GLMs. It expands fixed-trial-length limitations and possible remedies, and more explicitly acknowledges and motivates the strong timescale-separation assumption.

D1.justification: The code-access statement changes from an anonymous repository to Qi-Xin/GLM-Transformer. v2 supplies the added simulation's population sizes and connectivity. Existing hyperparameter, hardware, software and data-processing disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Brenner et al., Kirchmeyer et al. and Vermani et al., including Meta-Dynamical State Space Models in related work. A new component summary clarifies the relationships to DRS, NDT and reduced-rank regression.

P1.justification: v2 adds focused methodological explanations and expands the limitations discussion while preserving most prose and the main section sequence. It moves the checklist before the appendices, labels the animal-data section as Appendix G and improves appendix cross-references.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multipanel Figures S3 and S4, reformats Table S1 and redistributes existing figures across pages. The original main figures and Figures S1–S2 retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: The four-population ground-truth test strengthens support for scalability, while six-area outputs make the real-data evidence more inspectable. Clearer data requirements and trial-length limitations improve assessment of applicability. These are bounded gains; the unexplained Table S1 scale change remains a reporting drawback and prevents direct numerical comparison.
